paper_title: Faster Exponential-Time Approximation Algorithms Using Approximate Monotone Local Search
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
statement: ▶ Problem 6.1. Can an α-approximate algorithm running in time O∗ ((brute(α) − ε)n ) be derived from a parameterized extension β-approximation algorithm for any β > α?
context: Some interesting follow-up questions of our work are the following. ▶ Problem 6.1. Can an α-approximate algorithm running in time O∗ ((brute(α) − ε)n ) be derived from a parameterized extension β-approximation algorithm for any β > α? For example, for Directed Feedback Vertex Set only a parameterized 2-approximation algorithm running in time O∗ (ck ) [22] is currently available. The question is whether this algorithm can also be used to obtain an exponential 1.1-approximation algorithm that runs in time O∗ ((brute(1.1) − ε)n ), for some ε > 0? We also described and showed that the exhaustive search analog in the α-approximate n setting achieves the best possible running time of O∗ ((brute(α)) ) when one only has access to a membership oracle for the problem. Observe that for α = 1, SETH asserts that (brute(1))n = 2n is tight.
